name: Ava Landscapes LLC
website: avalandscapes.com - domain resolves but serves a generic '404 - Page not found' page, so there is effectively no website
what_they_do: Landscaping contractor doing landscape design and installation, lawn care, plant-bed care and pruning, sod and seeding, retaining walls, walkways, ponds and lighting. Run by owner Fred Albert with a crew, per reviews on third-party review sites.
customers: Homeowners in Spotswood and the surrounding Middlesex County area needing design/install projects and ongoing lawn and bed maintenance.

size_signals.signal: Owner Fred Albert plus a crew, described in reviews; service list covers design, lawn care, hardscape and lighting
Mon-Sat 8am-5pm hours published on a directory listing; accepts credit cards
4.9 from 34 reviews on HomeAdvisor and 4.8 from 36 on the Birdeye aggregate

listing.platform: HomeAdvisor (4.9/34); Birdeye aggregate 4.8/36; BBB profile exists and is not accredited

website_review.online_booking_or_quote: none - the listed domain is a 404, so the only paths are phone (908-309-6990) and third-party directories
website_review.out_of_date_signs: The website listed on the business's own directory profiles (avalandscapes.com) returns a bare '404 - Page not found!' page with no branding, no phone number and no link back - the domain is live but nothing is published on it
website_review.search_basics: Nothing to assess - no site exists, so no titles, descriptions, service pages or schema; searches for the business surface only directories (BBB, HomeAdvisor, Angi, YellowPages)
top_issues: Website is a dead 404 page while directory profiles still advertise it, which actively damages credibility for a homeowner comparing bids
No online quote request: every enquiry is a phone call to the owner, who is on site during the 8-5 working day
No owned portfolio - landscaping sells on photos, and the only images live inside third-party review profiles
No schema, no service pages, no service-area text anywhere the business controls

agent_readiness.notes: Findable: the business appears on multiple directories (HomeAdvisor, Birdeye, BBB, YellowPages) with consistent name, address and phone, which suggests a Google profile exists, but nothing could be confirmed directly and the listed website is dead. Answerable: nothing is published on an owned domain - no services, hours, service area or pricing in readable text, and no schema.org markup anywhere. Bookable: no form, no calendar and no working website, so a customer's agent cannot request a quote at all.

operations_signals.signal: Phone-only intake for a crew that works Mon-Sat 8-5 in the field, so calls during work hours are the main leak (inference from hours plus owner-crew model)
Reviews praise immediate call-back and clear scheduling; the differentiator is responsiveness, which currently depends entirely on Fred personally

top_opportunities.opportunity: Replace the 404 with a small portfolio site: service pages (design/install, lawn care, hardscape, lighting), job photos, service-area towns, hours, click-to-call and a labelled quote form with photo upload
top_opportunities.evidence: avalandscapes.com returns '404 - Page not found!'; directories still link to it

top_opportunities.opportunity: Missed-call text-back plus a quote-intake agent that captures address, project type, budget range and photos, then books a site visit
top_opportunities.evidence: No form or calendar anywhere; owner-crew working 8-5 Mon-Sat answers the phone personally

top_opportunities.opportunity: Google Business Profile and review pipeline: post project photos, add services and hours, and request reviews after each job (reviews are the current strength - 4.9/34 - and are not being compounded)
top_opportunities.evidence: Strong third-party ratings but no owned web presence to convert them

scores.reasons: Gap: website is a 404, so findability, answerability and bookability are all at zero. Pay: small owner-crew landscaping business; design/install jobs are a few thousand dollars, so budget is limited but a few jobs pay for the work. Ease: a portfolio site plus a form is a short, well-understood build. Evidence: the 404 is confirmed directly; everything else rests on third-party profiles, and the Google listing could not be opened.
